The original BERT4Rec paper already includes last-item-only training examples to reduce the mismatch with appended-[MASK] inference; it specifies no 50:50 ratio or random-prefix sampling distribution. Equation 8 averages cross-entropy over masked targets **within each example**. Thus terminal masking is established; a particular mixing ratio and prefix sampler are experimental choices. [Original paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690#S3.SS6)

The authors’ public implementation constructs sliding history windows, generates `dupe_factor` random-mask variants, and shuffles examples. Each window selects positions uniformly without replacement, with target count `min(max_predictions_per_seq, max(1, round(length × masked_lm_prob)))`; the default `mask_prob=1` replaces every selected item with [MASK]. Random selection includes terminal positions. Importantly, the published generator invokes `force_last=False` for training and `force_last=True` for evaluation; it does not explicitly implement the paper’s additional terminal-training mixture. Its loss flattens batch targets and divides summed cross-entropy by total valid-target weight, excluding padding—**per-target batch averaging**, despite the variable name `per_example_loss`. [Generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data.py), [loss implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py)

For the proposed single-model mixture, let example i have m_i targets and mean target loss a_i. Algebraically, per-example averaging is Σa_i/B: exactly balanced example counts give terminal and interior branches equal coefficients. Per-target averaging is Σ(m_i a_i)/Σm_i: with one terminal target and k interior targets per example, branch coefficients become 1/(1+k) and k/(1+k), respectively. Variable mask counts additionally favor examples containing more targets. To make “50:50” reproducible, use `0.5*mean(terminal_losses) + 0.5*mean(interior_per_example_mean_losses)` and specify prefix-endpoint sampling, mask eligibility, rounding/caps, and zero-target handling.
